payload.message:
The wrong deductions come from two things that only show up in the 5‑player layout:

- In the flow `Lichtloser_OnHit`, the 5‑player switch deliberately has no branch for `hitGroup == 5` (joker). If a hit with group 5 slips through, `hitPlayerIndex` is left at the previous value and you subtract the last player’s score at random. You can see the 5‑player mapping at `firmware/eez/src/v8pitteromat.eez-project` around the switch that tests `hitGroup >= 34 && ...` / `6..12` / `13..19` / `20..26` / `27..33` – group 5 is not mapped.

- Group 5 should never appear when the joker is off: both ESP planning and the Mega skip it only if the Mega knows that there are 5 players. The Mega skip is guarded by `currentPlayerCount == 5` in `firmware/arduino/MEGA/MEGA.ino:758`, but `currentPlayerCount` stays at its default `0` (`MEGA.ino:135`) unless it receives `CFG_PLAYERS …` (`MEGA.ino:832`). The current ESP code never sends that command (search `src/main.cpp`: no `CFG_PLAYERS`; older `src/main.cpp.bak:303` did). When player count changes to 5, the Mega still thinks it’s e.g. 0/6, doesn’t skip the joker segment, and occasionally lands on group 5; the flow then reuses the last `hitPlayerIndex`, causing the “S5 → S1/S5” and similar mis‑deductions.

What to do:
1) Send the player count to the Mega again whenever the player mode changes or at spin start, e.g. re‑add `rs485SendLine("CFG_PLAYERS %u\n", playerCount);` in `src/main.cpp` alongside the other spin config commands.
2) (Optional safety) In `Lichtloser_OnHit`, bail out when `playerCount == 5 && !jokerEnabled && hitGroup == 5` so a stray joker hit cannot reuse the previous player index.

With the Mega knowing `currentPlayerCount == 5`, it will skip group 5 when joker is off and the flow will no longer see joker hits, so points will be deducted correctly again.
